name: EtcdServer.compactRaftLog
existing_go_test: no (the derived raft panic was reproduced by the project's own tests, issues/etcd-compact-past-raft-applied.md)
note: As stated, false by framing: it writes raft's MemoryStorage (Compact), owned by raft's goroutine; the spec's pure part is trivial. The consequence found later (compaction past raftLog.applied, raft's hasUnappliedConfChanges panics on a campaign in that window) is observable, but only as a panic in raft's goroutine under an interleaving: a whole-server stress/fault test, not a per-call check of this spec.

name: EtcdServer.snapshot
note: Framing: CreateSnapshot on raft's MemoryStorage, WAL SaveSnap/Release, all unowned. No pure post to violate. Same downstream bug as compactRaftLog.

name: EtcdServer.applyConfChange
refuting_execution: applyConfChange with a ConfChangeAddNode whose Context is not a Member's JSON (e.g. "x") or an unknown change type: lg.Panic in ValidateConfigurationChange/applyConfChange. Also (c): RemoveNode of the local member (TestApplyConfChangeShouldStop does this) deletes it from the members map, contradicting membership.localKept if the checker's post includes it.
test_input_needed: malformed ConfChange context bytes; RemoveNode(self); a server state with a cluster
opaque_predicates: isServer (server state: its abstraction to a record)
existing_go_test: partly: TestApplyConfChangeShouldStop (server_test.go:367) removes the local member (part c); no upstream test of the malformed-context panic found
note: Part (a), applying the change to raft without node.ApplyConfChange's premise, is not observable (ghost/protocol).

name: EtcdServer.createMergedSnapshotMessage
note: Framing: commits the backend, opens a bbolt read tx streamed by a goroutine, writes m.Snapshot and reads *confState, all unowned; the return is correct Go behavior.

name: EtcdServer.revokeExpiredLeases
note: Permit premise: it proposes LeaseRevoke without reqPropOk (outside the KV workload invariant). The Go behavior is etcd's intended one; nothing in one execution contradicts a pure post (it takes and returns nothing).

name: EtcdServer.raftRequestAlarm
note: A second contract of raftRequest for every request without reqPropOk: a protocol/permit gap. Go proposes and returns normally; the falsity is that a proof can break the KV model's invariant.

name: EtcdServer.monitorStorageVersion
existing_go_test: no for the axiom; the related Go bug (issues/etcd-backend-duplicate-put-stale-read.md) has a project reproduction
note: Framing: writes meta/storageVersion under the apply thread's batch lock. Underneath it is a real Go bug, observable by a call sequence on the backend (three UnsafePut of one key in one batch tx, then a ReadTx read returns the oldest value), which a sequence fuzzer over the backend's specs could catch, but not through this monitor's trivial post.

name: EtcdServer.monitorKVHash
test_input_needed: CorruptCheckTime != 0 configuration (to even take the branch)
note: Reads the whole backend unowned and may propose Alarm{CORRUPT} without a permit; its pure part is trivial, so no execution refutes it.

name: EtcdServer.monitorCompactHash
test_input_needed: CompactHashCheck feature on
note: Unowned reads and an unpermitted CORRUPT alarm proposal.

name: EtcdServer.monitorDowngrade
test_input_needed: DowngradeCheckTime != 0 and a downgrade enabled
note: Proposes DowngradeInfoSet without a permit.

name: EtcdServer.Cleanup
refuting_execution: Cleanup, then a request goroutine (not in s.wg) uses the KV/backend through predicates that stayed persistent (e.g. mvcc store Compact -> Schedule panics 'schedule to stopped scheduler', or a backend read after be.Close).
test_input_needed: a call sequence Cleanup; Range/Put/Compact on the same server, with the checker treating the persistent store/backend predicates as still held
opaque_predicates: isBackend (persistent predicates the trace checker must carry across calls)
note: The falsity is in the persistence of other predicates (the stores' invariants keep describing them as live); observable only if the checker tracks which persistent facts remain established and then sees a later call panic.

name: EtcdServer.Alarm
note: The pre is raftRequest's without reqPropOk; Go proposes and returns fine. The falsity is a protocol premise of the KV model.

name: time.Since
refuting_execution: time.Since(t) with a clock that did not advance (coarse monotonic clock, e.g. Windows) returns 0, or a t without a monotonic reading (t.Round(0)) after a wall-clock step back returns a negative duration; the spec says 0 < d.
test_input_needed: clock control: a frozen or coarse clock, or wall-clock stepping with monotonic readings stripped
note: Partly single-call: time.Since(time.Now().Round(0)) can already give d <= 0 on a coarse clock; a negative d needs a wall-clock step. The fork's fix removed the axiom (Perennial's proved wp_Since).
